intended_object: A sub-action: a subset of M that is closed under the scalar action of R, i.e. c • x ∈ S whenever x ∈ S. This comes from the docstring and the name. Through `to_additive`, the additive version `AddSubAction` is defined at the same time.
explanation:
The structure consists of a carrier set `carrier : Set M` and the closure condition `∀ c x, x ∈ carrier → c • x ∈ carrier`. That is exactly a subset stable under the action, so it matches the docstring.

It only assumes `[SMul R M]`, with no requirement that the action be a monoid action, which is the weakest setting in which the notion makes sense. Mathlib builds more specialised notions on top of it, such as `Submodule`, which extends `SubMulAction`.

The empty set is allowed as a sub-action. This is the usual convention for invariant subsets, so it is not a degenerate-case error.

This declaration is itself Mathlib's definition of the notion, so there is no other Mathlib counterpart to cite.
